judge_reasoning: The model's solution follows the same strategic core as the official solution: Cartouche of Zeal on Alley Strangler to make one 5-toughness flier unable to block, Harmless Offering to give away Alley Strangler (causing the Cartouche to fall off via SBA and enable Revolt), Fatal Push to destroy the other 5-toughness flier using Revolt, and attacking with Glorybringer (exerted to kill Drana's Emissary) plus Goldnight Castigator for 8 unblockable flying damage, which is exactly lethal. All mana costs, targeting, and rules interactions (particularly the Revolt trigger via the Aura's SBA-induced graveyard trip) are handled correctly. The model simply makes a specific choice between the two symmetric 5-toughness fliers (Olivia and Drana) where the official solution left the choice ambiguous, so this is not a meaningfully different solution.
model_solution:
1. Tap a Mountain: cast Cartouche of Zeal enchanting Alley Strangler. ETB trigger: target Olivia, Mobilized for War — it can't block this turn.
2. Tap Mountain + 2 Swamps: cast Harmless Offering targeting the opponent and Alley Strangler. The opponent gains control of Alley Strangler. Cartouche of Zeal is now attached to a creature we don't control (illegal for "enchant creature you control"), so as a state-based action it is put into our graveyard — a permanent left the battlefield under our control, enabling Revolt.
3. Tap the last Swamp: cast Fatal Push targeting Drana, Liberator of Malakir (mana value 3, ≤4 with Revolt). Drana is destroyed.
4. Go to combat. Attack with Glorybringer and Goldnight Castigator (both flying). Exert Glorybringer; its trigger deals 4 damage to Drana's Emissary (4/4), destroying it.
5. The opponent's remaining creatures are Olivia (can't block this turn) and Alley Strangler (no flying or reach, can't block flyers). No blocks are possible. Glorybringer (4) + Goldnight Castigator (4) deal 8 combat damage: opponent goes from 8 to 0.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the board state: 5 lands giving RR BBB, opponent at 8 life with three flying threats (Olivia, Drana, Drana's Emissary), and our side featuring Alley Strangler and Glorybringer plus other creatures I need to account for.

My hand holds Harmless Offering, Fatal Push, Heart-Piercer Manticore, and Cartouche of Zeal. The key combo idea is giving away Goldnight Castigator via Harmless Offering so its damage-doubling effect works against the opponent, meaning just 4 damage would finish them off through Glorybringer's flying haste attack — though the three flying blockers complicate that.

I'm checking mana costs: Harmless Offering plus Cartouche of Zeal plus Fatal Push uses exactly my 5 available mana, but Fatal Push without revolt can't hit anything with mana value above 2, and all their creatures are MV 3, so I need to figure out how to trigger revolt.

Nothing under my control seems to leave the battlefield naturally this turn except through Heart-Piercer Manticore's sacrifice ability, but that costs 4 mana on its own, which doesn't fit the budget alongside everything else. I'm now weighing whether Glorybringer's exert ability could clear a blocker instead — 4 damage kills Drana's Emissary but not Castigator or Drana herself, and Cartouche of Zeal could stop Olivia from blocking, though Drana would still be able to block. I'm also considering whether Alley Strangler's menace matters here since the opponent has three creatures capable of double-blocking, and running the numbers on sacrificing Glorybringer to Heart-Piercer Manticore for a direct 4 damage hit while Castigator sits on the opponent's side, doubling that damage to 8 — exactly enough to end the game.

Checking that plan: opponent still has two blockers so they'd just block Castigator with one and let Strangler through for only 2, or double-block Strangler and take 4 from Castigator — either way it's not lethal, so that line fails too.

Let me reconsider giving Castigator away with Harmless Offering instead, seeing what that opens up for the opponent's board.

Giving Glorybringer's exert damage to opponent-controlled Castigator just makes it a doubled 8 damage, but it's a 4/9 so it survives — not useful. Harmless Offering targeting the Manticore isn't productive either. I need to find what actually deals 4 damage directly to the opponent after this exchange.

Working through the Cartouche and offering combos: giving away Castigator with Cartouche on Glorybringer to remove a blocker, exerting to kill Emissary, still leaves Drana and Castigator as blockers — Fatal Push can't kill either since neither has a low enough mana value without revolt. That line fails. I'm now wondering if Fatal Push could target my own creature to somehow enable something, though that doesn't trigger revolt on its own.

Then I realize the key trick: if Cartouche of Zeal is attached to Castigator and I then give Castigator away via Harmless Offering, Cartouche becomes illegally attached to a creature I no longer control, so it gets sacrificed as a state-based action — that's a permanent leaving the battlefield under my control, which enables revolt. So the plan is Cartouche of Zeal on Castigator to disable a blocker, then Harmless Offering Castigator away to trigger the Cartouche's fall and enable revolt.

Now with revolt active, Fatal Push can kill something up to MV 4 — Drana or Castigator or Emissary. I'm mapping out the combat math: Glorybringer attacks and exerts to burn down Emissary before blockers are declared, Fatal Push removes Drana, and I check what's left among Olivia (can't block), Castigator, and any remaining threats to see if the attack gets through.

With one blocker left, Strangler still can't get through since it needs two blockers absent, so opponent blocks Glorybringer and takes only 4 from Strangler — not lethal. I try reworking the Cartouche target, maybe hitting Strangler instead so it stays unblocked, but that loses revolt; I'm still searching for a way to make the exert trigger work.

Sacrificing Castigator to Manticore's ETB would deal only 4 damage, not enough on its own, so I keep looking for a combo that generates revolt and lethal damage simultaneously, considering whether giving the opponent a creature via Harmless Offering could set up a better sequence — though that doesn't trigger Olivia's ability.

Opp still lands at 2. Manticore has no haste so its ETB damage doesn't help this turn, and Cartouche for haste costs too much mana. Let me reconsider which creature to Fatal Push and how to sequence the exert/Cartouche targeting to squeeze out the last points of damage.

Since Harmless Offering is sorcery-speed, I need to cast it precombat instead: give away Castigator with Cartouche on it first so Olivia can't block, triggering revolt when Cartouche dies. Then attacking with Glorybringer and Strangler, opponent's remaining blockers are Drana and the gifted Castigator — if they leave Strangler unblocked it deals 4, dropping them to 4 life, not quite lethal yet.

Trying Fatal Push post-blocks doesn't unblock anything, so that's a dead end. Redirecting Glorybringer's exert damage to Drana instead of Castigator won't kill her either since she has 5 toughness, and Fatal Push plus exert on Castigator still falls one point short of its 9 toughness unless combat damage stacks onto it too — which is circular since that's exactly what I'm trying to arrange. Embalm isn't available without graveyard fuel, and swapping Cartouche onto Glorybringer or Offering onto Glorybringer doesn't make sense either, so I'm rechecking my mana — 5 lands total, Offering costs 3, plus Cartouche's cost.

I'm mapping out a Manticore + Cartouche line: put Cartouche on Manticore for haste and to make one opposing creature unable to block, then use Manticore's ETB to sacrifice Castigator for 4 damage to the opponent, dropping them to 4 life. Then attack with Glorybringer exerting to kill Emissary, plus hasty Manticore and menace Strangler — with only one blocker left (say Drana) after Cartouche, the opponent can't stop enough damage to survive, since Strangler alone gets through unblocked and either Glorybringer or Manticore also connects for lethal, though I need to double check the mana costs work out for casting Manticore before Cartouche.

But then I run into a mana problem: Manticore costs 2 generic plus RR, using both Mountains and two Swamps, which leaves no red source for Cartouche's R cost — I only have 2 Mountains total for 3 red mana needed, so this line fails.

Trying Manticore plus Fatal Push instead: cast Manticore off 2 Mountains and 2 Swamps, sac Castigator for 4 to the opponent (down to 4), triggering revolt, then Fatal Push kills Olivia or Drana. Attacking with Glorybringer (exerted to kill Emissary) and Strangler since Manticore lacks haste here, the remaining blocker stops Glorybringer while Strangler's 2 damage only brings them to 2 — not lethal.

I'm also considering using Manticore's sacrifice trigger to deal 4 damage to a creature instead of the opponent, checking which of their creatures that would actually kill.

Looking at their board with its counters: Olivia is 5/5, Drana is 4/5, Emissary is 4/4, so the Harmless Offering plan doubling Castigator seems like the intended route — I need to push 4 damage through up to four blockers using Glorybringer's 4 and Strangler's 2 menace. Exert kills Emissary, Push kills one via revolt from Cartouche falling off, and Cartouche's can't-block effect handles another, but one blocker still remains to stop Glorybringer unless I pump Strangler with Cartouche to double it to 6, which still isn't 8. I'm now wondering if the trick is casting Fatal Push after blockers are declared, leaving only Drana and Castigator to block while Olivia can't and Emissary is dead from exert.

If Drana blocks Glorybringer while Castigator stays back, Strangler gets through for 4 doubled damage but Glorybringer stays blocked since there's no trample, so pushing Drana post-block doesn't help. I try another sequencing — killing Drana pre-combat, exerting to kill Emissary, and Cartouche-stopping Olivia — but Castigator still blocks Glorybringer and the plan fails. I consider not giving away Castigator and instead attacking with it directly: with Castigator, Glorybringer, and Strangler swinging for a total of 10 against an opponent with three blockers, but even after removing blockers with Cartouche, exert, and a blocked Drana, the unblocked total only reaches 6, still short of the 8 needed, so I'm circling back to whether Harmless Offering targeting Strangler or Glorybringer instead changes the math.

Olivia's trigger seems irrelevant since no creatures would enter under the opponent's control, and Drana's ability doesn't apply here either. I think about doubling the Manticore's damage with Castigator for 8 lethal, but that costs 7 mana and I only have 5. I wonder if there's a way to push Castigator's toughness just high enough that the exert damage kills it, or whether Cartouche could enable a revolt-based Fatal Push in some other sequence, then start reconsidering whether the opponent is actually forced into a specific blocking assignment given their remaining creature.

Looking at how Strangler's doubled damage plays out if the single blocker takes Glorybringer instead, I keep landing at the opponent sitting at 4 life either way. I reconsider giving them Castigator and having it block Glorybringer, since the combined combat and exert damage would easily kill Castigator, but that still doesn't get damage through to the opponent's life total, so it doesn't solve the real problem.

Giving Cartouche to the opponent doesn't work since it requires "enchant creature you control" — since Castigator isn't theirs, Cartouche just dies without triggering revolt properly under our control. That path seems dead too.

Reconsidering Manticore with Push: sacrificing Castigator via Manticore's ETB deals 4 damage to any target, taking opponent from 8 to 4, and then Push with revolt can kill any of their creatures at MV 4 or less.

Testing this against their board with Glorybringer, Strangler, Olivia and Emissary though — none of the combinations quite close out the game since Olivia survives and can block. So the Manticore lines aren't working either, which pushes me back toward the Harmless Offering approach.

Since Strangler has menace and needs two blockers, if the opponent splits blockers either way, one attacker gets through for at least 4 damage.

I count only three neutralizers so far: Cartouche, Push, and exert on Emissary. But wait—Cartouche's ETB could target Castigator itself before it changes hands, making it unable to block regardless of who controls it after Harmless Offering transfers it.

Even so, running through the attack sequence still leaves one blocker free—whoever survives blocks Glorybringer while Strangler's doubled damage isn't enough to close it out, so I need to rethink the ordering of attacks and effects entirely.

Working through the block assignments: if Drana blocks Glorybringer opponent drops to 2, if she blocks Castigator opponent drops to 1, but either way I don't have enough mana left for Manticore since Cartouche ate my extra Mountain. Trying the alternate line without Cartouche: attack with all three, exert kills Emissary, they block the two fliers leaving Strangler's 2 damage through, dropping opponent to 6, then I'd have 4 mana post-combat for Manticore.

Checking whether Castigator or Glorybringer survive their blocks though—Olivia's doubled damage kills Castigator, and Drana's first strike kills Glorybringer, so both blocked attackers die and Manticore sacrificing Strangler only gets 2 damage through, which isn't enough. Holding Fatal Push for combat doesn't help since revolt isn't active. Considering Harmless Offering on Castigator so it can block Glorybringer instead, but Glorybringer has no trample so that doesn't matter either.

I'm trying Fatal Push for revolt via a sacrifice, but that only affects our own permanents and none of them have low enough mana value to die to Push. Reconsidering the Harmless Offering plus Cartouche plus Push line, but Push would kill Castigator before the doubling effect applies, so that fails too. Drana's Emissary's upkeep trigger isn't relevant since it's not our turn. I'm going back to recheck the blocker scenario involving Cartouche's ETB targeting.

Working through the Harmless Offering line: Cartouche stops Drana from blocking, Push kills Olivia, exert kills Emissary, but Castigator can still block Glorybringer, leaving Strangler to deal 4. I check whether skipping the Glorybringer attack helps, but it doesn't, and Glorybringer's exert never targets the opponent directly anyway. I also consider whether Castigator's damage-doubling combined with Push could work, but Cartouche can't be on both Glorybringer and Castigator at once for revolt purposes.

Then it clicks: put Cartouche on Strangler instead, and Offering that same Strangler to the opponent — the Cartouche falls off, triggering revolt, while Castigator stays on our side. Now the opponent sits at 8 life, and Glorybringer plus Castigator deal exactly 4+4=8 unblocked, since Strangler can't block flyers and Cartouche, Push, and exert clear out the other three blockers entirely. The mana works out too — Cartouche and Offering both cost red plus generic, Push just needs black, all covered by our Mountain and Swamps.

Strangler's menace doesn't matter here since it's not blocking; Olivia's trigger only fires on entering, not on control change, so switching control is safe. I could also target Drana with Cartouche and Push Olivia instead — either order works fine as long as revolt still triggers.

For the Aura legality question, rule 704.5m says an Aura not properly attached goes to its owner's graveyard, and "enchant creature you control" requires the Aura's controller to control the enchanted creature — I want to double-check that against the actual rule text.

content.content:
1646:303.4c If an Aura is enchanting an illegal object or player as defined by its enchant ability and other applicable effects, the object it was attached to no longer exists, or the player it was attached to has left the game, the Aura is put into its owner’s graveyard. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)
4748:702.103e As a bestowed Aura spell begins resolving, if its target is illegal, it ceases to be bestowed and the effect making it an Aura spell ends. It continues resolving as a creature spell. See rule 608.3b.
4750:702.103f If a bestowed Aura becomes unattached, it ceases to be bestowed. If a bestowed Aura is attached to an illegal object or player, it becomes unattached and ceases to be bestowed. This is an exception to rule 704.5m.
5486:704.5m If an Aura is attached to an illegal object or player, or is not attached to an object or player, that Aura is put into its owner’s graveyard.
6457:801.8. An Aura can’t enchant an object or player outside its controller’s range of influence. If an Aura is attached to an illegal object or player, the Aura is put into its owner’s graveyard as a state-based action. See rule 704.
